solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Protective panel pal's contrived with barrel in cabin

indicators.note: something contrived is artificially made up, so the letters before it are rearranged
one piece sits in another, so the barrel goes inside the cabin

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
a shack is a rough cabin
b. is a dictionary abbreviation for barrel

explanation.surface: A friend has rigged up some protective panelling with a barrel inside a hut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pal's contrived' reads as a friend's handiwork, but the possessive just supplies four letters to rearrange; B for barrel is a dictionary abbreviation rarely seen outside barrel measures.
explanation.definitionFit: A splashback is the panel behind a sink or cooker that shields the wall from spills.

clue.text: Poet's family shield that includes clubs on the spot

indicators.note: a word that includes something holds it inside, so clubs goes within

blocks.note: such and that are interchangeable in 'such a thing' / 'that kind of thing'
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
in, as in present or at home

explanation.surface: A family coat of arms showing clubs is displayed right there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poet' here means Spenser, whose spelling of scutcheon this is; 'that includes clubs' looks like a description of the shield but is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Scuchin is Spenser's form of scutcheon, an escutcheon or heraldic shield bearing a family's arms.

clue.text: Youngster grips us, hot for exercise in gym

indicators.note: something that grips holds what follows in its grasp, so it goes inside

blocks.note: a pup is a young animal, or a cheeky youngster
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A youngster grabs hold of the speaker and others, all sweaty from a gym workout.
explanation.walkthrough: The pair of pieces goes inside the young animal's name after its first letter, splitting it into P and UP.
explanation.definitionFit: A push-up is a floor exercise lowering and raising the body with the arms, a gym staple.

clue.text: Landed with some long boring list

blocks.note: lit is a past tense of light, to land or come to rest
as in 'have you any?'

explanation.surface: Someone arrives saddled with a long, tedious list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Landed' looks like arriving or acquiring; it is the past tense of light, as a bird lights on a branch.
explanation.definitionFit: A litany is a prayer of repeated petitions, and by extension any tediously long recital or catalogue.

clue.text: Treads rashly in paths spoiling one of gaiters

indicators.note: acting rashly is acting wildly, so these letters are thrown about
spoiling ruins the original order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stamps carelessly over footpaths, ruining one of their gaiters.
explanation.walkthrough: Two indicators, one for each word, combine into a single eleven-letter rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Spatterdashes were long leggings or gaiters worn to keep mud off; they came in pairs, so this is one of them.

clue.text: Arab covering to hitch to the ears

indicators.note: what reaches the ears is what is heard, not what is written

blocks.note: to hitch up is to hike up

explanation.surface: Someone lifts an Arab robe up as far as the ears.
explanation.definitionFit: A hyke, or haik, is a large outer wrap of cloth worn by Arabs over the head and body.

clue.text: Crane or rook interrupting a festival

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so the piece goes inside

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the chess notation for rook
a gala is a festive occasion

explanation.surface: A crane or a rook gate-crashes a festival, as birds will.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crane or rook' reads as a pair of birds; only crane defines, and rook is the chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The argala is the adjutant bird, a large Indian stork-like crane.

clue.text: Old bloke accepts new form of retrial linked to another

indicators.note: a new form of a word reshapes it, so its letters are rearranged
to accept is to take in, so the rearranged letters go inside

blocks.note: cove is old slang for a man or chap
taken as written

explanation.surface: An elderly man agrees to a fresh retrial connected with another case.
explanation.definitionFit: Correlative means mutually related, so each of a pair is bound up with the other.

clue.text: George is one working without control, independent in scheme

definitions.text: George is one working without control
definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the noun: George is the nickname for an automatic pilot

indicators.note: placed in something means put inside it

blocks.note: I is the abbreviation for independent
a plot is a scheme

explanation.surface: A man named George works without supervision, acting independently within a plan.
explanation.walkthrough: George is the traditional airmen's name for an aircraft's automatic pilot, which flies with no hand on the controls.
explanation.definitionFit: An autopilot is a type of pilot, steering a craft with nobody manning the controls.

clue.text: Entertain American in almost half his home

indicators.note: almost half keeps only three of seven letters, dropping the rest
in places the first piece inside the second

blocks.note: the American's home country
US, as in a US citizen

explanation.surface: Someone entertains a visiting American in a part of his house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his' refers back to the American, so his home is AMERICA; three of its seven letters, AME, hold US.
explanation.definitionFit: To amuse someone is to entertain or divert them.

clue.text: Unfinished anthem, a very small thing

indicators.note: something unfinished lacks its ending, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: a motet is a short sacred choral anthem

explanation.surface: An incomplete anthem is a very small affair.
explanation.definitionFit: A mote is a speck, like a particle of dust in a sunbeam.

clue.text: Scottish git whenever led by copper

indicators.note: being led by something means it comes in front

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
if in the sense of whenever, as in 'if it rains, we stay in'

explanation.surface: A Scottish idiot whenever a policeman is in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a policeman but is the metal, with its chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuif is a Scots word for a fool or lout, a dialect equivalent of a git.

clue.text: April first traps bovine creature

definitions.note: proximo means of next month, so in a March letter it stands for April

indicators.note: a trap encloses its catch, so the creature goes inside

blocks.note: primo is Italian, and musical, for first
an ox is a bovine animal

explanation.surface: An April Fool's prank snares a cow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'April first' looks like April Fool's Day; April is the definition alone. In old business letters, 'the 5th proximo' meant the 5th of next month.
explanation.definitionFit: Proximo means in the coming month, so written in March it refers to April.

clue.text: Returning buggies maybe driven from tee at Turnberry?

indicators.note: returning means going back the way one came, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: karts, like golf buggies, are small motorised vehicles

explanation.surface: Golfers driving back in their buggies after teeing off at Turnberry.
explanation.walkthrough: Turnberry is a golf course in Scotland, pointing to a Scots word. The surface hides the fact that 'driven' is the definition, not the buggies.
explanation.definitionFit: Strak is a Scots past tense of strike, so a ball struck off the tee in Scotland.

clue.text: Latticework structure made of timber, badly fitted inside

indicators.note: fitted inside says one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: a tree is timber on the stump
ill as an adverb means badly

explanation.surface: A garden lattice built of wood has been poorly installed.
explanation.definitionFit: A treille is a trellis, a framework of crossed strips for training plants.

clue.text: Excess creating start of lipoma in stomach

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter
in places the selected letter inside the next word

blocks.note: the gut is the stomach
opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Too much fat causes a fatty lump to begin forming in the belly.
explanation.walkthrough: A lipoma is a benign fatty tumour, which fits the picture of excess around the stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: A glut is an oversupply, more than is needed.

clue.text: Beloved, if old tenor joined in – one such?

definitions.note: refers back to the clue: one who has joined in the singing

indicators.note: pieces joined in something are put inside it

blocks.note: cher is French for dear, beloved
an is an archaic word for if
T is the abbreviation for tenor

explanation.surface: Darling, had the old tenor joined the chorus, would he be one of them?
explanation.walkthrough: 'One such' points back to the tenor who joined in, i.e. someone singing a chant; 'if old' signals the archaic sense of a short word.
explanation.definitionFit: A chanter is a person who chants, like the singer who joined in the chorus.

clue.text: Sandstone came into view with potassium in

indicators.note: with something in means it is placed inside

blocks.note: something that arose appeared
K is the chemical symbol for potassium

explanation.surface: A sandstone bed appeared, rich in potassium.
explanation.definitionFit: Arkose is a sandstone with a high feldspar content, which is notably rich in potassium.

clue.text: To seek possible rentier, make a show of head-rhymes? (13, three words)

blocks.note: to hunt is to seek
one who lets property, who may live on rents

explanation.surface: A search for someone living on rents is presented in showy alliteration.
explanation.walkthrough: A letter here is one who lets, a landlord; a rentier lives on such income, hence 'possible'.
explanation.definitionFit: Head-rhyme is alliteration, and to hunt the letter is to overdo alliteration for effect.

clue.text: Jockey Lester, accepting tribunal's conclusion, gives fresh account

indicators.note: to jockey is to manoeuvre, so the letters are moved about
accepting takes something in
a conclusion is an ending, so only the final letter is used

blocks.note: taken as written
final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Jockey Lester Piggott, having heard the tribunal's verdict, tells his story again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jockey Lester' reads as Lester Piggott, the famous British jockey, but jockey is the verb that scrambles his name.
explanation.definitionFit: To retell something is to give an account of it again.

clue.text: Dishes, alas, I ruined HM swallowed

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so these letters are jumbled
what is swallowed goes inside

blocks.note: taken as written
Her Majesty is ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A cook laments ruining the dishes the Queen ate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dishes' looks like food; here it means satellite dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Satellite dishes are aerials, devices for receiving broadcast signals.

clue.text: A tricky fence? Point for each

blocks.note: a ras is a headland or cape
per means for each, as in 'per head'

explanation.surface: A difficult fence, with a point awarded for each one cleared.
explanation.definitionFit: In hunting, a rasper is a stiff, difficult fence to jump.

clue.text: Seaside clan, swimming? This with seals possibly can impart stings

indicators.note: swimming letters float about and settle in a new order
possibly says the answer plus some letters could be one rearrangement of the earlier words

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; these letters are the rest of the mix

explanation.surface: A family of seals swimming at the seaside could be stung by jellyfish.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite: the answer plus SEALS is a rearrangement of SEASIDE CLAN, so take those five letters away and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Cnidae are the stinging cells of jellyfish and similar animals, which discharge threads that sting.

clue.text: Training requires such sustenance, spanning time

indicators.note: something spanning another stretches across it, so it surrounds it

blocks.note: meals provide sustenance
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Physical training calls for proper food, taken over time.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Training' as train-ing, running trains: the rails are called the metals.
explanation.definitionFit: Railway lines are known as the metals, and trains cannot run without them.

clue.text: Lodestone from North America: gun metal fashioned with art (13, two words)

indicators.note: fashioned means shaped anew, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: NA is the abbreviation for North America
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lodestone from America, crafted with artistry out of gunmetal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lodestone is magnetite that is naturally magnetised, the original natural magnet.

clue.text: Show concern (as some do) when ring's concealed in palm

indicators.note: what is concealed is no longer seen, so those letters vanish

blocks.note: people who show concern are caring
taken as written

explanation.surface: People fret when a ring is hidden in someone's hand.
explanation.walkthrough: '(as some do)' turns 'show concern' into 'are caring'; hide RING from the end and ARECA remains. 'Palm' suggests a hand but is the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The areca is a genus of palm, including the betel-nut palm.

clue.text: Link husband added to necklace

blocks.note: a torc is a twisted metal neck ring
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A link with a husband joined on to a necklace, like a chain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Link' looks like a chain link; it is the old word for a torch of pitch carried through streets.
explanation.definitionFit: A link was a torch of pitch and tow once carried to light the way.

clue.text: Loose women? They're popular with sailors

blocks.note: first meaning: American slang for women, often disparaging
second meaning: Norfolk's lakes and rivers, much used for boating

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests women of the port, but the second sense is the Norfolk Broads, a network of waterways in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Broads is slang for women, and the Norfolk Broads are a favourite region for yachting.

clue.text: Book one doing time for robbery

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for book
a lag is a convict

explanation.surface: A prisoner is charged with robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like charging a suspect; it is the abbreviation. An old lag is British slang for a habitual convict.
explanation.definitionFit: Blag is British slang for a robbery, especially a violent one.

clue.text: Hard part of cell, on strike, leading to end of enterprise

indicators.note: leading to something means coming before it
the end of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: a light that is on is lit
to hit is to strike
final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Part of a cell block, with the workers on strike, ends the business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on strike' reads as an industrial action phrase, but the two words give separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A lithite is a hard calcareous concretion in a sensory cell, a stony particle used for balance.

clue.text: Fellow (with terrible reputation?) removing daughter from bed

indicators.note: removing takes something away from the word that follows

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
a divan is a kind of bed

explanation.surface: A man with a bad reputation drags a daughter from her bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket hints at Ivan the Terrible, the Russian tsar.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan is a man's name, borne most famously by Ivan the Terrible.

clue.text: Larval discharge secreted in taller pines

indicators.note: secreted means tucked away, so the answer lies within the next words

blocks.note: runs across the two words

explanation.surface: Grubs ooze a substance which collects in taller pine trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'secreted' plays on secretion, which suits the discharge but here means hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: Lerp is a sweet waxy secretion produced by the larvae of certain Australian insects on leaves.

clue.text: Dried meat, food without stuffing in a way?

indicators.note: with its stuffing gone the word keeps only its outer letters
in places the remaining letters inside the next word

blocks.note: via means by way of
food emptied of its middle

explanation.surface: Dried meat is food that needs no stuffing, in a sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without stuffing' sounds culinary but asks for the inside letters of food to be removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Vifda is a Shetland term for meat dried in the open air without salt.

clue.text: Charger most curse in race running wild

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its last letter
running wild means out of control, so these letters scatter
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
to cuss is to curse

explanation.surface: A warhorse swears a lot as it bolts out of control during the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charger' looks like a horse; it is someone who brings a charge.
explanation.definitionFit: An accuser is one who charges another with wrongdoing.

clue.text: Others addressed by southerners recalled song line

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: a lay is a song or ballad
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Southern folk remembered a line from a song for everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: The southerners are those of the southern United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Y'all, short for you all, is the southern US way of addressing a group of other people.

clue.text: Around end of reign the loser's wretched … this?

definitions.text: Around end of reign the loser's wretched … this?

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter
wretched means in a sorry state, so the letters are wrecked
around says one piece wraps another

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
final letter of the word

explanation.surface: When a monarch's reign ends, the deposed loser is miserable at being this.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer: a deposed ruler, his reign over, is left without a throne.
explanation.definitionFit: Throneless means without a throne, as a deposed monarch is once the reign is lost.
